# Motion Studio

The studio lives at `motion-studio/` in the `ahmadscb/ahmad` repository (VPS: wherever it is cloned). Design rules come from the **bang-motion** plugin skill. Read its `SKILL.md` (anti-PPT laws, style brief, camera) and, for characters, `references/kartun-panggung.md`. This skill adds production: rendering, sound, QC and limits.

## Workflow (do all of it; never stop at a storyboard)

1. Write `projects/<name>/brief.json` (schema `workflow/brief.template.json`):
   - format, type, **style** (one of the six in `lib/styles.js`), message;
   - script/dialogue, cast (from the 10 library characters), sets;
   - a shot-by-shot storyboard with times, sfx and music.
2. Scaffold with `bin/bm-new <name> --dur <s> --template cartoon` (character stories) or `--template reel` (type and graphics).
   Then build `index.html` from the **asset library** (`workflow/LIBRARY.md`):
   - `BM.CH` characters, expressions, poses and actions;
   - `BM.ENV` sets and `BM.PROP` props;
   - `BM.CAM` moves and `BM.TR` transitions;
   - `BM.say` / `BM.CAP` for subtitles and bubbles;
   - `BM.STYLE` style packs;
   - `BM.sfx` / `BM.music` for sound.
   
   Draw new things only when the library lacks them. 3D: `lib/product3d.js` (see `projects/aether-ad`).
3. **Dialogue:** write `dialogue.json` and run `python3 tools/voice.py projects/<name>/dialogue.json projects/<name>/voice`.
   - It's a free local voice per character, with lip-sync visemes.
   - Time the shots from `voice/dialog.json`.
4. Run `node tools/snap.mjs projects/<name> /tmp/check <times…>` and **look at `sheet.jpg`** (Read the image). Fix:
   - clipped or overlapping text;
   - off-model characters;
   - empty or slide-like frames;
   - props hidden behind other layers.
   
   Repeat until clean.
5. Run `bin/bm-render projects/<name> --voice projects/<name>/voice/dialog.wav` (omit `--voice` if there's no dialogue; `--blur 2` adds motion blur).
6. Inspect frames taken **from the MP4** (`ffmpeg -i out/<name>.mp4 -vf fps=1/1.5,scale=216:-1,tile=10x2 -frames:v 1 sheet.jpg`) and read `out/qc.txt`. Repair and re-render until clean.
7. Report the MP4, `out/render-metrics.json` (time, peak RAM, peak CPU), and what was checked.

## Guardrails

- Zero paid APIs by default. ElevenLabs needs `--allow-paid`, plus `allow_paid` in the brief, plus an environment key. Never print or store keys.
- Never publish. Renders run under `bin/bm-safe` (memory cap, CPU cores, low priority). Don't touch other services.
- Determinism: no `Math.random`, no clocks, no network during render (fonts, GSAP and three.js are vendored).
- Never put a `//` comment in the middle of a line of code. It disables the rest of the line.

## References

- **Sarcastic Grotesque** (face-first reaction-meme comedy, separate cast of 10 with 33 deforming expressions): `workflow/GROTESQUE.md`, `templates/grotesque`; agent: `bin/bm-agent "<brief>" --style grotesque --run`.
- **Library API:** `workflow/LIBRARY.md`. Visual catalog: `library/catalog`. Six-style showcase: `library/styles`.
- **Worked examples:** `templates/cartoon` (library demo with voice), `projects/crypto-crash` (2D comedy), `projects/aether-ad` (3D product ad).
- **Sound:** `tools/sound.py` (53 effects, 12 music styles, two-pass −14 LUFS).
- **Voice:** `tools/voice.py` (local Piper/LibriTTS-R, CC BY 4.0) and `tools/lipsync.py` (audio to visemes).
# Motion Studio pipeline: prompt to MP4

Each stage has one owner (the agent or a script) and one artefact, so another agent (Hermes, a scheduler, a human) can take over at any boundary.

| # | Stage | Owner | Artefact |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Creative brief** | agent | `projects/<name>/brief.json` (schema: `workflow/brief.template.json`) |
| 2 | **Style brief + storyboard** | agent, following the Bang Motion `SKILL.md` | `brief.json` → `style_brief`, `storyboard[]` (t0/t1, shot, camera, text, sfx, music) |
| 3 | **Scaffold** | `bin/bm-new <name> --dur N --template cartoon\|reel` | `projects/<name>/index.html` (bm-core + library, local GSAP/fonts) |
| 4 | **Visual assets** | agent | asset library first (`workflow/LIBRARY.md`: 10 characters, 9 sets, 17 props, 6 styles); new SVG only when missing; 3D via `lib/product3d.js` |
| 5 | **Animation** | agent | the GSAP timeline: stages + cameras, `BM.sfx()` and `BM.music()` cues next to the visual they belong to |
| 6 | **Dialogue / narration** (optional) | `tools/voice.py dialogue.json voice/` (characters, local) or `tools/narration.py` | `dialog.wav` + `dialog.json` (line timings + lip-sync visemes). ElevenLabs only with `--allow-paid` |
| 7 | **Key-frame QC** | `node tools/snap.mjs projects/<name> out/check t1 t2 …` | `sheet.jpg`. The agent **looks** at it: clipped or overlapping text, off-model character, slide feel, empty frames |
| 8 | **Render** | `bin/bm-render projects/<name> [--voice vo.wav] [--blur 2]` | `out/<name>.mp4`, `render-metrics.json` (resource-limited by `bin/bm-safe`) |
| 9 | **Video QC** | `tools/qc.sh` (run by bm-render) + agent inspects frames **from the MP4** | `qc.txt`. Spec, black/frozen frames, loudness (−14 LUFS) |
| 10 | **Repair loop** | agent | fix → 7 → 8 → 9 until clean |
| 11 | **Export** | done | MP4 H.264/AAC, yuv420p, +faststart. **Publishing is not wired** (human review first) |

## Rules the agent must keep

- **Determinism:** every frame is a function of `t`. No `Math.random` (use `BM.hash`), no clocks, no network at render time.
- **Rigs:** joints use `BM.J`. GSAP never touches a joint's `transform`. The placement group and the animated group are separate elements.
- **Vertical (9:16) layout:** stack the story (screen above character, character above desk) instead of side by side. Keep camera zoom ≥ 1.05.
- **Sound:** every visible action that needs a sound gets a `BM.sfx` cue at the same `t`. Music sections are named styles.
- **Comments:** never put a `//` comment in the middle of a line of code. It silently disables the rest of the line (this broke two renders during testing).

## Integrations (prepared, not enabled)

- **ElevenLabs:** `tools/narration.py --provider elevenlabs --allow-paid`, plus `narration.allow_paid: true` in the brief, plus `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` in the environment.
- **Hermes / other agents:** write `brief.json`, then call `bin/bm-agent "<prompt>" --name X --run`, which runs headless Claude Code with a tool allowlist. Read `out/render-metrics.json` and `out/qc.txt`.
- **Instagram / TikTok:** deliver `out/<name>.mp4` (1080×1920, 30 fps, −14 LUFS). Auto-publishing is deliberately absent.
- **TOYA product ads:** start from `projects/aether-ad` (3D product + kinetic type). Swap the model for the real product (glTF) and the brand palette.
- **SlideSpoken explainers:** start from `projects/crypto-crash` (rig + expressions + stages). Bang Motion's explainer starters cover the 16:9 educational styles.

# Sarcastic Grotesque: face-first reaction-meme comedy `lib/grotesque.js` (`BM.GR`) is a **separate** character system: the simple `BM.CH` puppets are untouched. Use it when the brief asks for sarcastic, ugly-funny, meme-style or reaction comedy. The face is the punchline. - **Template:** `bin/bm-new --dur 20 --template grotesque` - **Sheets:** `library/grotesque/sheets/` - **Style pack:** `BM.STYLE.use('grotesque')` (Anton meme subtitles) Load order: ```html ``` ## The cast (original characters, fixed identities) Each character has a default attitude (their **base**), a distinct head silhouette, nose, teeth and voice. | id | who | look | base | |---|---|---|---| | `gary` | exhausted office employee | long droopy egg head, comb-over, eye bags, stubble, coffee-stained shirt | dead inside | | `brock` | smug boss | wide boxy jaw, helmet hair, mustache, double chin, navy suit | smug | | `kyle` | fake motivational manager | spray-tan, spiky blond quiff, headset, giant veneers, "TEAM LEAD" lanyard | fake smile | | `vlad` | dramatic crypto trader | big potato head, bulging bloodshot eyes, mop and cowlick, gold ₿ chain, hoodie | panic | | `tiff` | gossip girl | pointy heart-shaped chin, lashes, glossy lips, ponytail, hoops | side-eye | | `bev` | judgmental auntie | jowly box head, curlers, red cat-eye glasses on a chain, chin mole, pearls | judgmental | | `zeke` | weird influencer | split teal/pink mullet, ring-light eyes, crooked nose, tiny mustache, neon tank | psycho smile | | `marco` | broke guy acting rich | long narrow face, slick hair, sunglasses on head, pencil mustache, gold tooth, chipped fake chain | overconfident | | `dale` | overconfident salesman | huge shiny forehead dome, side tufts, cleft chin, horse teeth, plaid blazer | overconfident | | `pip` | chaotic best friend | frizzy orange hair, buck teeth with a gap, freckles, band-aid, stripes | manic laugh | To build one, call `ch = GR.make(stageGroup, id, x, y, scale)`. - `(x, y)` is the **head centre**. The bust (shoulders and chest) hangs below, so put a desk or frame edge over the lower body. - Scale 1 gives a head about 470 px tall. ## Expressions (33): `GR.expr(ch, at, name)` morphs; `GR.react(ch, at, name, opts)` snaps Every expression actually reshapes the face: jaw length, eye size per eye, lid angles, mouth shape, crooked teeth, gums, tongue, wrinkles, folds and colour overlays. They aren't brow tweaks. The expressions, by group: - **Smug and sly:** smug, plotting, evilGrin, sarcasticClap, passiveAggro, overconfident, judgmental. - **Fake:** fakeSmile, fakePro, psychoSmile. - **Shock and fear:** shockScream, panic, terrified, whatDidISee, caughtLying, overwhelmed. - **Negative:** disgust, cringe, jealous, suspicious, sideEye, embarrassed. - **Broken:** deadInside, done, sleepyBroken. - **Crying:** uglyCry, hystericalCry, heartbreak. - **Rage:** angryMeltdown, unhingedRage. - **Manic:** manicLaugh, greedy. - **Reset:** neutral. Plain-English aliases also work, for example `'dead inside'`, `'caught lying'` or `'full unhinged rage'`. Some expressions bring hands automatically: | Expression | Hands | |---|---| | panic, terrified | hands on cheeks | | angryMeltdown, unhingedRage | fists | | plotting | steepled fingers | | sarcasticClap | slow clap | | greedy | rubbing hands | | overwhelmed | grabbing head | | embarrassed | scratching head | | heartbreak | hand on chest | | fakePro | adjusting tie | | overconfident | thumbs up | | caughtLying | shrug | Call `GR.hands(ch, at, preset)` to set them yourself. The presets are rest, cheeks, grabhead, facepalm, clap, fists, steeple, shrug, chest, rub, thumbs, point, scratch, tie, phone, selfie and temples. ## Animation behaviour | Call | What it does | |---|---| | `GR.react(ch, at, name, {sc, shot, pop, sfx, smear, hands})` | **The reaction shot**: anticipation squash (0.12 s) → snap with overshoot → squash/stretch pulse, head jerk and smear ghosts → elastic settle. With `sc` it also punches the camera (`shot`: close, ecu or mouth). Default sfx is `boom` | | `GR.pop(ch, at, hold)` | eyes pop out, pupils pinpoint | | `GR.jawDrop(ch, at, amt, hold)` | jaw falls with a bounce and the skull stretches | | `GR.blink`, `GR.jerk(ch, at, dx, dy)`, `GR.recoil` | exaggerated blink, head jerk, recoil | | `GR.smear(ch, at)` | smear frames | | `GR.tremble(ch, t0, t1, amp)`, `GR.wobble(ch, t0, t1)` | shaking, lip wobble | | `GR.tearBurst(ch, t0, t1)` | tear fountains | | `GR.hold(ch, t0, t1)` | **comedic hold**: stops idle drift and blinks, so the face freezes | | `GR.laugh(ch, t0, t1)` | manic bouncing laugh | | `GR.clap(ch, t0, t1, rate)` | slow sarcastic clap, synced to clap sfx | | `GR.escalate(ch, t0, ['panic', 'terrified', 'hystericalCry', 'unhingedRage'], .55)` | rapid escalation, each step a snap | | `GR.slide(ch, at, dx, dur)` | bust walks in or out with a bob | | `GR.say(ch, t0, t1, text, {visemes})` | lip-synced talking on top of any expression, plus a meme subtitle | ## Shot grammar (use it; it's what makes this style funny) 1. **Framing** is set per character with `GR.frame(ch, kind)`, where kind is wide, medium, close, ecu (eyes) or mouth. - Hard cut: `GR.cutTo(sc, at, ch, kind)`. - Snap zoom with whoosh: `GR.punch(sc, at, ch, kind)`. - Creep-in on a hold: `GR.drift(sc, t0, dur)`. 2. **The beat:** 1. **SETUP** in medium (1–2 s, a normal moment). 2. **TRIGGER** (something happens; sfx). 3. **SNAP REACTION:** `GR.react` with a punch to close or ecu, plus `GR.backdrop(ch, at, dur, 'speed'|'burst'|'rage'|'dread')`. 4. **COMEDIC HOLD** of 0.6–1.2 s (`GR.hold`). 5. **Hard cut** to the next beat. 3. **Coverage:** - At least 50 % of screen time is close-ups or ECUs. - Cut every 1.2–2.5 s. - No wide shot lasts more than 2 s. - Every video has at least three snap reactions. 4. **Contrast normal and absurd.** Stay calm and quiet right before the face explodes. Silence or crickets work before the boom. 5. **The punchline is a face.** End on an ECU reaction plus a meme caption (`GR.meme(at, dur, 'TEXT', {pos: 'top'})`) and a comedic sound (boom, rimshot, cricket, trombone, wrong, dun). 6. **Escalation.** Repeat the gag with bigger faces each time (rule of three), or use `GR.escalate`. ## Sets and props - **Sets:** `GR.BG.office(p)`, `GR.BG.desk(p, x, y)`. - **Reaction backgrounds:** `GR.BG.burst`, `.speed`, `.dread`, `.rage`, `.void`. - **Monitor:** `m = GR.monitor(p, x, y, s, {key: GR.SCREENS.meme|spreadsheet|crash|off})`. Switch screens with `m.flip(at, key)`. - **Captions:** `GR.meme(at, dur, text)` for top/bottom meme text; `GR.label(at, dur, '9:01 AM')`. - **Other places:** build any other set with plain SVG (`BM.R`, `BM.PA`) using **thick ink outlines (#16110E, stroke 7–9) and muted, dirty colours**. Draw the set behind the characters, and any foreground (desk, car door, phone frame) after them. ## Sound - **Comedy sfx:** - impacts and cues: boom, zoom_in, punch, dun, wrong, gong; - camera and face moves: whoosh, slide_down, slide_up, eyepop; - comedy reactions: rimshot, cricket, trombone, gasp, laugh, squish; - hands and objects: clap, keys, notify, register. - **Music:** awkward, drama, sneaky, tension, hype, sad. - **Mix:** keep the music low (gain 0.5–0.7). The face sfx carry the jokes. ## Quality gate (check before accepting a render; iterate if any answer is "no") 1. Is every reaction readable at phone size within 0.5 s, from the face alone? 2. Do the faces actually deform (jaw, eyes, mouth shape), or did only the brows move? 3. Are at least half the frames close-ups or ECUs, with at least three snap reactions? 4. Is there a calm "normal" beat before each absurd face? 5. Does the video end on a face punchline with a held frame of at least 1 s? 6. Is there nothing cute or plain on screen: every character in a strong attitude, never idle-neutral for long? __TITLE__

Everything is deterministic and seek-safe. ## Characters: `BM.CH` The same id gives the same look in every scene and every video. | id | who | look | |---|---|---| | `dave` | office guy / trader | spiky brown hair, blue hoodie | | `maya` | designer | black bob, coral T-shirt, glasses, earrings | | `omar` | manager / boss | bald, beard, navy suit, red tie, wide build | | `lina` | consultant | teal hijab, cream blazer | | `kenji` | developer | slick black hair, dark T-shirt, red headphones | | `grace` | senior colleague | grey bun, purple cardigan, glasses | | `leo` | kid | red cap, yellow T-shirt, freckles (short) | | `sam` | intern | curly hair, green hoodie, lanyard | | `rex` | CEO | black suit, gold tie, mustache, wide build | | `zara` | athlete / creator | ponytail, purple T-shirt, earrings | ### Building a character - `ch = CH.make(parent, id, x, groundY, scale, {mode:'flat'|'ink'|'line', legs:true})` builds the rig. - Feet sit at (x, groundY). A full figure is about 600×scale px tall. - `legs:false` gives a bust, for behind desks. - The rig's joints are: - `ch.root` (x/y move the whole character; sx/sy squash); - `ch.torso`, `ch.head`; - `ch.Rarm`, `ch.Rfore`, `ch.Larm`, `ch.Lfore`; - `ch.Rthigh`, `ch.Rshin`, `ch.Lthigh`, `ch.Lshin`. Animate them with `BM.jto(j, at, {r|x|y|sx|sy}, dur, ease)`. Never animate `transform` directly. - **Expressions** (`CH.expr(ch, at, name)`, 23 of them): - positive: neutral, smile, happy, laugh, smug, ecstatic ($-eyes), sly, love, wink, proud, starstruck; - fear and surprise: shock, panic, scared, nervous; - negative: sad, cry, angry, furious, deadpan, confused, sleepy, disgusted. Extras switch on automatically: tears, sweat, anger vein, zzz, "?", blush, sparkles. - **Poses** (`CH.pose(ch, at, name, dur)`, with built-in anticipation, overshoot and settle; `CH.snap` sets one instantly): - neutral, wave, point, pointUp, armsUp, handsHips, crossArms; - thinking, facepalm, shrug, thumbsUp, typing, phone, clap; - hideFace, presenter, sip, stretch, sneak. - **Actions:** - locomotion: `CH.walk(ch, at, dur, dx)`, `CH.run`, `CH.sneak`; - sitting: `CH.sit(ch, at, seatDrop)`, `CH.stand`; - big moves: `CH.jump`, `CH.celebrate`, `CH.cry(ch, t0, t1)`, `CH.dance(ch, t0, t1, bpm)`; - small moves: `CH.typing(ch, t0, t1)`, `CH.nod`, `CH.shakeHead`, `CH.startle`, `CH.fall`. - **Life:** - `CH.idle(ch, t0, t1)`: breathing, head drift and blinks. Write `projects//dialogue.json` with `{"lines": [{"who": "omar", "text": "..."}, ...], "duration": 30}`. - Add `"t0"` to a line to pin it to a time; otherwise lines run in sequence with `gap`. 2. In the page, add ``. Then, for each line, call `BM.say(CH_BY_ID[l.who], l.t0, l.t1, l.text, {visemes: l.visemes})`. - **Time the visuals from `DIALOG.lines`**, not from guesses. 4. Render with `bin/bm-render projects/ --voice projects//voice/dialog.wav`. 5. Credit line for descriptions: "Voices: Piper / LibriTTS-R (CC BY 4.0)". `tools/lipsync.py any.wav` turns any voice file into visemes. ## Sound: `BM.sfx(t, type, gain)` and `BM.music(t0, t1, style, gain)` - **Effects (53):** - comedy: boing, bonk, trombone, rimshot, cricket, laugh, gulp, slurp, slurp_empty, squeak, twitch, gasp, spit, scratch, fall, sting, drumroll; - movement: whoosh, swoosh, step, tiptoe, door, zip, creak, flutter; - hits: punch, thud, hit, impact, crack, crash, shatter, sub_drop; - devices and UI: keys (typing), notify, ding, pop, tick, glitch, shutter, alarm, horn, buzz; - money: coin, register, cash_tiny; - ambient: rain, heartbeat; - premium: riser, swell, shimmer, glint, paper. - **Music (12):** - comedy and light: sneaky (comic tiptoe), cartoon, lofi, lofi_broke; - mood: sad, tension, cinematic; - upbeat: hype, corporate, pulse; - specialised: edu, product. ## Styles: `BM.STYLE` `BM.STYLE.use('cartoon'|'premium'|'edu'|'comic'|'infographic'|'product3d')` returns the style pack: palette, fonts, subtitle style, easing, character mode, preferred transitions, music and components. Switch screens with `m.flip(at, key)`. - **Captions:** `GR.meme(at, dur, text)` for top/bottom meme text; `GR.label(at, dur, '9:01 AM')`. - **Other places:** build any other set with plain SVG (`BM.R`, `BM.PA`) using **thick ink outlines (#16110E, stroke 7–9) and muted, dirty colours**. Draw the set behind the characters, and any foreground (desk, car door, phone frame) after them. ## Sound - **Comedy sfx:** - impacts and cues: boom, zoom_in, punch, dun, wrong, gong; - camera and face moves: whoosh, slide_down, slide_up, eyepop; - comedy reactions: rimshot, cricket, trombone, gasp, laugh, squish; - hands and objects: clap, keys, notify, register. - **Music:** awkward, drama, sneaky, tension, hype, sad. - **Mix:** keep the music low (gain 0.5–0.7). The face sfx carry the jokes. ## Quality gate (check before accepting a render; iterate if any answer is "no") 1. Is every reaction readable at phone size within 0.5 s, from the face alone? 2. Do the faces actually deform (jaw, eyes, mouth shape), or did only the brows move? 3. Are at least half the frames close-ups or ECUs, with at least three snap reactions? 4. Is there a calm "normal" beat before each absurd face? 5. Does the video end on a face punchline with a held frame of at least 1 s? 6. Is there nothing cute or plain on screen: every character in a strong attitude, never idle-neutral for long? __TITLE__

I rendered the video and it passed QC. It's a 20-second vertical cartoon of the crypto trader losing everything, told mostly through his face, and the frames pulled from the MP4 look right.

**MP4:** `/home/user/Ahmad/motion-studio/projects/crypto-meltdown/out/crypto-meltdown.mp4`, 1080×1920 at 30 fps, exactly 20.0 s (600 frames), H.264 with AAC audio.

**QC (`out/qc.txt`):** passed. Format matches the spec, there are no black frames and no frozen stretches over 1.2 s, and loudness is −14.5 LUFS with a true peak of −1.3 dBTP.

**Render metrics (`out/render-metrics.json`):** 243.9 s wall time, 755 MB peak memory, 197% peak CPU (3 cores, 6 GB cap), exit code 0.

**The story:** Vlad, the crypto trader from the grotesque cast, sits in his bedroom at 3:14 AM saying "Diamond hands, baby" while his coin is up 420%. Each time the chart gets worse, his face gets bigger:
- −5%: a sweaty fake smile and "It's just a dip."
- −40%: he snaps into panic, with popping eyes and speed lines behind him.
- He tries denial with "Buy the dip!", rubbing his hands with dollar-sign eyes.
- −80%: a screaming extreme close-up, then he runs through terror, hysterical crying and full rage.
- His friend Pip (also from the cast) asks flatly "Bro. Did you sell?" and Vlad answers in silence: "I am the dip."
- The screen reads LIQUIDATED at 3:15 AM. Pip bursts out laughing.
- Last shot: Vlad's frozen psycho smile through tears, an eye-pop extreme close-up, the caption "HODL'D TO ZERO" and a sad trombone, held for about 3 s.

Both voices are free local ones, lip-synced and subtitled. The music drops out before the punchline.

**Quality gate (all yes):**
1. **Readable within 0.5 s from the face alone?** Yes. Every reaction snaps in and is backed by a camera punch and a backdrop.
2. **Do the faces really deform?** Yes. The jaw drops, eyes pop out at different sizes, and the mouth changes shape (square grimace, wide scream, tongue out), with tears and snot added.
3. **At least half close-ups, at least three snap reactions?** Yes. About 60% of screen time is close-ups or extreme close-ups, and there are 8 snap reactions.
4. **A calm beat before each big face?** Yes. Each dump is first shown on the monitor before Vlad reacts, and the call with Pip plus "I am the dip" play quiet before the final blow.
5. **Ends on a face held at least 1 s?** Yes. The final face is held for about 3 s, with the extreme close-up making up the last 1.7 s.
6. **Nothing cute or plain on screen?** Yes. Both characters hold a strong attitude the whole time.

**What I fixed after the snapshot checks:**
- **Pip's eye:** his phone hand covered one eye during his line, so I dropped the phone and lowered the WAGMI sign so it stays in frame.
- **Final shot:** the extreme close-up cut off the grin and showed part of the monitor in the corner. Now the grin shows in a close-up first, then the camera snaps to the eyes, and the monitor is hidden.
- **Opening shot:** I moved the camera so the monitor isn't clipped at the left edge.

The brief, dialogue and page are in `projects/crypto-meltdown/` (`brief.json`, `dialogue.json`, `index.html`). I didn't edit anything outside that folder and nothing was published.
